headline: 本週戲劇文學評論
context: 衛報本輪評論同樣橫跨影視與文學。恐怖選集劇《The Terror》最新一季把場景搬進破敗的精神病院，Dan Stevens主演；入圍布克獎的小說《The Disappearers》則直面牙買加的恐同社會現實；立陶宛返鄉電影《The Visitor》則描寫遊子重返故里的疏離心境。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Expect gory set pieces and jump scares galore in the return of the supernatural anthology series, with Dan Stevens among the many poor souls terrorised by an evil spirit haunting their ward Things that go bump in the night? Bad. Things that go bump in the night in a dilapidated psychiatric hospital? Infinitely worse. That, basically, is the premise of Devil in Silver, the latest volume of anthology series The Terror, which began in 2018 with a supernaturally charged tale of a polar expedition to find out what happened to Sir John Franklin’s voyage. Crikey, it does not end well. The next was set during the second world war and was about shapeshifters from Japanese folklore terrorising a Japanese-American community in southern California. A hiatus followed, but now The Terror is back with a double dose of horror: a malevolent spirit moving in and out of the bodies of the patients of New Hyde psychiatric hospital, and the more tangible but no less frightening diabolism of the US mental healthcare system. Pepper (Dan Stevens, still of Downton Abbey fame despite his many varied roles since) is in New Hyde because the three policemen who arrested him after they caught a few punches he was aiming at his girlfriend’s controlling ex threw him in there rather than completing the paperwork the station would have required. There he meets the lost and suffering souls who have ended up in what amounts, due to underfunding and understaffing, to a holding pen rather than a rehabilitative or care facility. Dorry (Judith Light) is the longest-serving resident – put there decades ago by her husband because of her endless crying fits, though her later memories reveal a greater darkness. Kofi (Chinaza Uche) – or Coffee, as he is called by the rest of his companions until it is too late – was a structural engineer in Ghana but now depends on medication to keep himself steady. Loochie (played by non-binary actor b) ended up in the system after a violent incident with a sibling, but at least one member of staff believes her charge is able to cope in the real world and, as the hospital’s evil spirit gathers strength and wrath, gets the chance to prove it. sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: This Booker-listed epic set in Aids-era Kingston is a triumph – bitter, bawdy and ravishingly queer “A sense of sweep,” replied Marlon James, when asked what moves him most in literature. “Sweep isn’t just about external journeys, but internal as well. It can be over years and decades, or across land and sea.” If that explanation is still hazy, pick up his mighty new novel, which is longlisted for this year’s Booker prize and is tirelessly – sometimes exhaustingly – grand and peripatetic. Mounting a grisly exposé of Jamaican homophobia, this polyphonic 640-page doorstopper is an emotionally bruising narrative that roves “uptown, downtown, ghetto and gully” through Aids-era Kingston with sidetrack excursions to 1950s England and a closing leap to 2000s United States. The novel’s defining event is a gruesome mob attack on eight queer men who have clandestinely come together to work on bringing John Herbert’s 1967 gay prison play, Fortune and Men’s Eyes, to the stage. The goal, in the words of director Havelock Titus, is to shatter “the whole fragile myth of Jamaican male sexuality”. “Because prison,” he explains, “is the ultimate male institution and yet masculine sexualities that could never happen outside in the normal world flourish in there all the time.” Continue reading...
sources.title: The Disappearers by Marlon James review – a scorching exposé of homophobia in Jamaica

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: This portrait by Vytautas Katkus of a man contemplating his recent fatherhood and his own father is steeped in ennui and ends up drifting At one point in this Nordic-Baltic homecoming film, Danielius (Darius Šilėnas) refuses an invite for beachfront karaoke, preferring to watch from behind a polythene partition. At another, a neighbour glimpses him exercising across the courtyard, through the window of the flat in an end-of-summer Lithuanian resort that Danielius is trying to sell. Having returned from Norway to settle up accounts, this prodigal son is often holding the world at arm’s length – and director Vytautas Katkus does his best to help him with this distanced technique in this quizzical and faintly existential drama. Little tangible is disclosed. Danielius is a thirtysomething father who skipped the funeral of his own dad the year before. Preparing the flat to go on the market, he walks the dog of his neighbour, Vismante (Vismantė Ruzgaitė), hangs speculatively at beach gatherings and falls asleep in pine forests. Ice-cream is eaten at every available opportunity. He’s not alienated exactly, but somewhat out of step. As he looks for new anchorage, even the film seems to question whether Danielius has sufficient main character energy: it periodically drifts to follow another resident, Tomas (Rokas Siaurusaitis), who is caring for his grandmother over the way. thread_text: 這輪評論一次橫跨恐怖劇、文學與電影。選集劇《The Terror》最新一季《Devil in Silver》把舞台搬進破敗的精神病院，Dan Stevens飾演一名被警察隨手關進院內的男子，在體制的失能與邪靈的雙重威脅下掙扎求生。入圍今年布克獎的小說《The Disappearers》，作者是Marlon James，故事設定在愛滋病肆虐年代的牙買加京斯敦，直面當地的恐同社會現實，全書長達640頁。立陶宛電影《The Visitor》則講一個從挪威返鄉的中年父親，賣掉老家公寓的過程中，重新面對自己與亡父的關係。
threads_text: 這輪評論橫跨恐怖劇、文學獎小說與返鄉電影，主題各異卻都在挖掘人與體制、人與過去的糾葛。選集劇《The Terror》睽違多年推出新一季《Devil in Silver》，場景搬進一間因資金與人力短缺而形同關人所的精神病院，Dan Stevens飾演一名因警方懶得走完程序而被隨手送進院內的男子，故事在體制失能與邪靈作祟之間來回拉扯。入圍今年布克獎的小說《The Disappearers》，作者Marlon James把640頁的篇幅，用來直面愛滋病年代牙買加京斯敦的恐同社會現實，書中一場對同志男性的私刑攻擊，是全書最核心的事件。另一邊，立陶宛電影《The Visitor》講一位從挪威返鄉、準備賣掉老家公寓的中年男子，如何在整理故居的過程裡，被迫重新面對與亡父之間懸而未決的關係。
voice_text: 換個口味，聊聊這幾天的戲劇跟文學評論。（停頓一下）先說恐怖劇。選集劇《The Terror》推出新一季，場景搬進一間資金短缺、形同關人所的精神病院，Dan Stevens飾演一個被警察隨手送進去的男人，故事在體制的失能，跟邪靈作祟之間來回拉扯。接著是小說。入圍布克獎的《The Disappearers》，作者用六百四十頁的篇幅，直面愛滋病年代牙買加的恐同社會現實，書裡有一場對同志男性的私刑攻擊，是整本書最核心的事件。最後是電影。立陶宛片《The Visitor》，講一個從挪威回鄉賣房的中年男人，怎麼在整理老家的過程裡，被迫面對自己跟過世父親之間，一直沒說開的心結。
